h1: Private Jet to Cabo San Lucas and Los Cabos
hero_sub: Desert mountains drop straight into the Pacific, humpbacks breach off the Arch in winter, and every sunset turns the granite copper.
answer: A private jet to Cabo takes about 2 hours 30 minutes nonstop from Toluca (AIT) to Los Cabos International (SJD), and starts at $3,800 USD one way on a Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers. The Challenger 605 and Gulfstream GV are quoted in 30 minutes for your dates. Every price is per aircraft and includes crew, fuel, catering and permits, and the route runs year-round.
story_title: Where the desert meets the sea
story: Los Cabos sits at the very bottom of the Baja California peninsula, 1,700 km from Toluca, where the Sea of Cortez finally opens into the Pacific Ocean. The flight northwest crosses the Sierra Madre and then a long stretch of open gulf. On approach the landscape turns to cardón cactus, granite and pale beaches that run for miles, and the first thing you notice when the door opens is the dry desert heat with a faint edge of salt.

Two towns share this coast. San José del Cabo is the quieter one, with a whitewashed mission church, a leafy plaza and an art district that holds a Thursday night art walk in season. Cabo San Lucas, about 30 km west along the Tourist Corridor, is the marina, the sportfishing fleet and the famous rock arch at Land's End. Between them, cliffside resorts and golf courses look out over a sea that Jacques Cousteau called the aquarium of the world.
why_title: Why charter a private jet to Cabo

why.d: Airline departures to Los Cabos run on a fixed schedule from a crowded terminal. From Toluca you choose the hour, arrive minutes before takeoff and land at SJD about 2 hours 30 minutes later, in time for sunset on the Corridor the same day you leave the office.

why.t: Room for golf bags and gear
why.d: Cabo trips come with luggage: golf clubs for Cabo del Sol or Puerto Los Cabos, fishing tackle, dive gear and a week of clothes for the whole family. On a private aircraft all of it flies with you, and the Challenger 605 seats up to 12 in a stand-up cabin.

A Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers starts at $3,800 USD one way, per aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. That is about $543 per seat with a full cabin. Larger aircraft such as the Challenger 605 and Gulfstream GV are quoted in 30 minutes.

At two and a half hours each way, a Thursday evening departure and a Sunday night return give you three full days in Baja. Domestic flights can be ready about 2 hours after confirmation, so a free weekend that appears on Wednesday is still very much on the table.

journey_title: From Polanco to the Tourist Corridor

journey.d: Close the laptop after an early lunch and head west toward Toluca on the México-Toluca highway. Count on about an hour in the car. An official photo ID is all you need for this domestic flight, so the paperwork is already done.

The car pulls up at the private terminal (FBO) at Toluca International. A quick ID check, your bags go aboard, and you are at the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes from the curb. There is no gate to find.

A late lunch or a cold drink as you climb out of the valley. The last part of the flight crosses the Gulf of California, and on a clear day the Baja peninsula appears ahead as a long brown line on the horizon.

Touchdown at Los Cabos International after about 2 hours 30 minutes. Baja California Sur runs one hour behind Mexico City, so you gain an hour of daylight. Your car is waiting on the private aviation side of the airport.

Fifteen minutes puts you in San José del Cabo, about forty-five in Cabo San Lucas. Check in, take a swim, and be on a terrace facing the water with a cold drink when the sun goes down over the Pacific.

places_title: What to do in Cabo after your private jet lands

places.name: El Arco de Cabo San Lucas
places.d: The granite arch at Land's End marks the spot where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific. Take a water taxi or a private boat from the marina, stop at Lover's Beach on the gulf side, and look for sea lions sunning on the rocks. In winter, humpback whales pass just offshore.

places.name: San José del Cabo
places.d: The older of the two towns grew around a Jesuit mission founded in 1730. Stroll the plaza, step inside the mission church, browse the galleries of the art district, then drive a few minutes into the hills of Animas Bajas for dinner at one of the farm restaurants among the fields.

places.name: Cabo Pulmo National Park
places.d: About two hours up the East Cape, this protected reef is one of the great marine conservation stories anywhere. Fish life came back in force after the area was protected in 1995, and divers and snorkelers now swim among huge schools of jacks, rays and reef fish in clear, warm water.

places.name: Todos Santos
places.d: About an hour north on the Pacific side, this Pueblo Mágico is all adobe streets, art galleries and surf breaks. Have lunch in town, browse the shops around the plaza, then sit on the sand at nearby Playa Los Cerritos and watch the surfers as the light goes gold.

best_time_title: Best time to fly to Los Cabos
best_time: Los Cabos is sunny and dry most of the year, so a private jet to Cabo works in any month. December through April is whale season, when humpback whales arrive from colder northern waters to breed and calve, and it is also the busiest stretch for private flights. Christmas, New Year and Semana Santa book up first, so send those dates early. May and June are hot, dry and calm. July through October brings heat, humidity and the chance of Pacific storms, and October is also the month of the big billfish tournaments out of Cabo San Lucas. November is warm and clear, a favorite with golfers.
airport: Your jet lands at Los Cabos International (SJD), just north of San José del Cabo and about 1,700 km from Toluca. Private aircraft are handled through the general aviation side of the airport, apart from the commercial terminals and their crowds, and your car can meet you there. Downtown San José is about 15 minutes away, the hotels of the Tourist Corridor 20 to 35 minutes, Cabo San Lucas around 45 and Todos Santos about an hour and a half. This is a domestic flight, so there is no customs stop.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Los Cabos
docs: Your flight to Los Cabos is domestic, so Mexican nationals only need a valid official photo ID, such as an INE card or a passport. Foreign visitors should carry the passport they used to enter Mexico. Send the full name of every passenger on WhatsApp when you confirm, and the aircraft can be ready about 2 hours later. Customs and immigration do not apply on this route.

faq.q: How much is a private jet to Cabo?
faq.a: A private jet to Cabo from Toluca starts at $3,800 USD one way on a Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers, per aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. The Challenger 605 for up to 12 and the Gulfstream GV for up to 16 are quoted in 30 minutes for your dates.

faq.q: How long is a private jet flight from Mexico City to Los Cabos?
faq.a: About 2 hours 30 minutes nonstop from Toluca (AIT) to Los Cabos International (SJD), 365 days a year. Baja California Sur is one hour behind Mexico City, so a 2:15 pm departure lands at about 3:45 pm local time, early enough for a swim before dinner.

An empty leg is a flight an aircraft has to make without passengers, usually to reposition after dropping off another client. Operators sometimes offer those legs below the normal charter price. The date and direction are fixed by the other trip, so they suit flexible plans. Ask JETCAB on WhatsApp whether one lines up with your dates.

faq.q: When is whale season in Los Cabos?
faq.a: Roughly December through April, when humpback whales gather off the tip of the peninsula to breed and calve. It is the peak season for private flights to Los Cabos, together with the Christmas holidays and Semana Santa, so confirming your aircraft early is the safest move.

faq.q: Do you tip a private jet pilot?
faq.a: It is never expected. Your JETCAB quote already covers the crew, along with fuel, catering and permits, so there is nothing extra to pay on the day. Some passengers leave a gratuity for the crew after a long weekend or a special occasion, and that is entirely your choice.

faq.q: Is Los Cabos accessible year-round by private jet?
faq.a: Yes. JETCAB flies the Toluca to Los Cabos route all year. Summer and early fall are hot and humid with the chance of Pacific storms, and the crew will advise you if weather affects a departure. Winter and spring bring the most stable flying weather and the busiest demand.
